Record its elapsed time in seconds and whether it # warned that the loss did not fall below the tolerance. optimize_once <- function(optimize, start, summary) {   warned <- FALSE   seconds <- system.time(     optimized <- withCallingHandlers(       optimize(start, summary, iterations = iterations, tolerance = tolerance),       retrogroup_warning = function(condition) {         warned <<- TRUE         invokeRestart("muffleWarning")       }     )   )[["elapsed"]]   list(optimized = optimized, warned = warned, seconds = seconds) }  # Pair each target with the achieved statistic of the same subgroup level. # Returns one row per subgroup level and quantity. compare <- function(targets, achieved) {   achieved <- achieved[     match(subgroup_label(targets), subgroup_label(achieved)),   ]   rows <- lapply(names(quantities), \(quantity) {     column <- quantities[[quantity]]     data.frame(       subgroup = subgroup_label(targets),       quantity = quantity,       target = targets[[column]],       estimate = achieved[[column]]     )   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  # One replication of one method, following steps 1 to 5 of the Design # section. Returns a list with estimates (one row per scenario, subgroup # level, and quantity) and runs (one row per scenario). replication <- function(method, colon) {   variables <- unique(colon$summary$variable)   # Step 1: ground truth.   truth <- method$sample(colon$patient, colon$summary)   # Step 2: targets.   targets <- group_analysis_summary(truth, variables)   # Step 3: starting point.   start <- method$sample(colon$patient, targets)   # Step 4: optimization. Each scenario shows the optimizer different inputs.   inputs <- list(     Available = targets,     Unavailable = transform(targets, standard_error = NA_real_)   )   results <- lapply(scenarios, \(scenario) {     run <- optimize_once(method$optimize, start, inputs[[scenario]])     # Step 5: comparison.     achieved <- group_analysis_summary(run$optimized, variables)     list(       estimates = cbind(scenario = scenario, compare(targets, achieved)),       runs = data.frame(         scenario = scenario,         warned = run$warned,         seconds = run$seconds       )     )   })   list(     estimates = collect(results, "estimates"),     runs = collect(results, "runs")   ) }  # Summarize the differences (estimate minus target) over replications: # means, plus the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles of the differences. # Returns one row per method, scenario, subgroup level, and quantity. summarize_estimates <- function(estimates) {   estimates$difference <- estimates$estimate - estimates$target   out <- stats::aggregate(     cbind(target, estimate, difference) ~       subgroup + quantity + scenario + method,     data = estimates,     FUN = mean   )   interval <- stats::aggregate(     difference ~ subgroup + quantity + scenario + method,     data = estimates,     FUN = stats::quantile,     probs = c(0.025, 0.975)   )   out$lower <- interval$difference[, 1L]   out$upper <- interval$difference[, 2L]   out }  # Run many replications of every method. Returns a list with estimates # (the output of summarize_estimates()) and runs (one row per optimization # run). benchmark <- function(colon, reps) {   by_method <- lapply(names(methods), \(name) {     results <- replicate(       reps,       replication(methods[[name]], colon),       simplify = FALSE     )     list(       estimates = cbind(method = name, collect(results, "estimates")),       runs = cbind(method = name, collect(results, "runs"))     )   })   estimates <- collect(by_method, "estimates")   runs <- collect(by_method, "runs")   # Factor levels fix the order of rows in tables and panels in figures.   estimates$method <- factor(estimates$method, levels = names(methods))   estimates$scenario <- factor(estimates$scenario, levels = scenarios)   estimates$quantity <- factor(estimates$quantity, levels = names(quantities))   estimates$subgroup <- factor(     estimates$subgroup,     levels = subgroup_label(colon$summary)   )   runs$method <- factor(runs$method, levels = names(methods))   runs$scenario <- factor(runs$scenario, levels = scenarios)   list(estimates = summarize_estimates(estimates), runs = runs) }  # Show 3 decimal places, but switch to scientific notation with 3 # significant figures for nonzero values that would otherwise round to zero. format_number <- function(x) {   ifelse(     x != 0 & round(x, 3L) == 0,     formatC(x, digits = 2L, format = "e"),     formatC(x, digits = 3L, format = "f")   ) }  # Label each combination of method and scenario, ordered by method and # then by scenario. panel_label <- function(method, scenario, sep) {   grid <- expand.grid(scenario = scenarios, method = names(methods))   factor(     paste0(method, sep, "SE ", tolower(scenario)),     levels = paste0(grid$method, sep, "SE ", tolower(grid$scenario))   ) }  show_table <- function(x) {   x <- x$estimates   # Rows of hr and se are in the same order because summarize_estimates()   # sorts by method, scenario, quantity, and subgroup.   hr <- x[x$quantity == "Log hazard ratio", ]   se <- x[x$quantity == "Standard error", ]   knitr::kable(     data.frame(       Method = hr$method,       `Standard errors` = hr$scenario,       Subgroup = hr$subgroup,       `Mean target log HR` = format_number(hr$target),       `Mean log HR` = format_number(hr$estimate),       `Log HR difference` = format_number(hr$difference),       `Mean target SE` = format_number(se$target),       `Mean SE` = format_number(se$estimate),       `SE difference` = format_number(se$difference),       check.names = FALSE     ),     align = c("l", "l", "l", rep("r", 6L)),     row.names = FALSE   ) }  show_plot <- function(x) {   x <- x$estimates   x$panel <- panel_label(x$method, x$scenario, sep = "\n")   ggplot(x, aes(x = difference, xmin = lower, xmax = upper, y = subgroup)) +     geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#8c8b86") +     geom_pointrange(color = "#2a78d6", size = 0.4) +     facet_grid(panel ~ quantity, scales = "free_x") +     scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +     labs(x = "Estimate minus target", y = NULL) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +     theme(       panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),       panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),       panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),       strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)     ) }  show_runs_table <- function(x) {   seconds <- stats::aggregate(     seconds ~ scenario + method,     data = x$runs,     FUN = \(s) c(stats::quantile(s, c(0.5, 0.95)), max(s))   )   warned <- stats::aggregate(     warned ~ scenario + method,     data = x$runs,     FUN = \(w) c(length(w), mean(w))   )   knitr::kable(     data.frame(       Method = seconds$method,       `Standard errors` = seconds$scenario,       Runs = warned$warned[, 1L],       `Median seconds` = format_number(seconds$seconds[, 1L]),       `95th percentile seconds` = format_number(seconds$seconds[, 2L]),       `Max seconds` = format_number(seconds$seconds[, 3L]),       `Fraction warned` = format_number(warned$warned[, 2L]),       check.names = FALSE     ),     align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 5L)),     row.names = FALSE   ) }  show_runs_plot <- function(x) {   runs <- x$runs   runs$panel <- panel_label(runs$method, runs$scenario, sep = ", ")   runs$warned <- factor(     ifelse(runs$warned, "Warned", "Converged"),     levels = c("Converged", "Warned")   )   ggplot(runs, aes(x = seconds, y = panel)) +     geom_jitter(       aes(color = warned),       height = 0.2,       width = 0,       size = 0.6,       alpha = 0.4,       show.legend = TRUE     ) +     geom_boxplot(fill = NA, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +     scale_x_log10() +     scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +     scale_color_manual(       values = c(Converged = "#2a78d6", Warned = "#d6542a"),       name = NULL,       drop = FALSE     ) +     guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +     labs(x = "Elapsed seconds per optimization (log scale)", y = NULL) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +     theme(       legend.position = "top",       panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),       panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()     ) }

Estimates from repeated calls to one sampler on one dataset: # one row per sampled dataset, subgroup level, and quantity. sample_estimates <- function(sampler, data, reps) {   summary <- data$summary   variables <- unique(summary$variable)   key <- paste(summary$variable, summary$level)   # Array of estimates: subgroup level x quantity x sampled dataset.   fits <- replicate(reps, {     sample <- sampler(data$patient, summary)     estimates <- group_analysis_summary(sample, variables)     rows <- match(key, paste(estimates$variable, estimates$level))     as.matrix(estimates[rows, quantities])   })   subgroup <- paste0(summary$variable, ": ", summary$level)   rows <- lapply(names(quantities), \(quantity) {     data.frame(       subgroup = factor(subgroup, levels = subgroup),       quantity = factor(quantity, levels = names(quantities)),       target = summary[[quantities[[quantity]]]],       estimate = c(fits[, quantities[[quantity]], ])     )   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  # Benchmark every sampler on the same list of datasets. # Returns one row per sampler, subgroup level, and quantity. benchmark <- function(datasets, reps) {   estimates <- lapply(names(samplers), \(name) {     estimates <- lapply(       datasets,       \(data) sample_estimates(samplers[[name]], data, reps)     )     cbind(       sampler = factor(name, levels = names(samplers)),       do.call(rbind, estimates)     )   })   estimates <- do.call(rbind, estimates)   estimates$difference <- estimates$estimate - estimates$target   out <- stats::aggregate(     cbind(target, estimate, difference) ~ subgroup + quantity + sampler,     data = estimates,     FUN = mean   )   interval <- stats::aggregate(     difference ~ subgroup + quantity + sampler,     data = estimates,     FUN = stats::quantile,     probs = c(0.025, 0.975)   )   out$lower <- interval$difference[, 1L]   out$upper <- interval$difference[, 2L]   out }  simulate_dataset <- function(n) {   beta <- c(-0.8, 0, 0.5)   levels <- c("low", "middle", "high")   treatment <- stats::rbinom(n, 1L, 0.5)   x <- sample.int(3L, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.4))   event_time <- stats::rexp(n, 0.1 * exp(beta[x] * treatment))   censor_time <- stats::runif(n, 0, 20)   patient <- tibble::tibble(     treatment = treatment,     time = pmin(event_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(event_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(levels[x], levels = levels)   )   summary <- group_analysis_summary(patient, "group")   patient$group <- NULL   list(patient = patient, summary = summary) }  #
